identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

page_refs.doc_date: page 1, header row shows September 2026; last entry is Sep 17

scan.summary: A shift-by-shift inspection log for a Toyota propane-powered forklift at the Portland warehouse, recording pre-shift safety checks required by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). The log documents operator inspection of tires, wheels, forks, carriage, chains, mast, hydraulics, horn, lights, seat belt, brakes, steering, propane tank security, fire extinguisher, data plate, and overhead guard, with pass/fail marks for each shift. Any defects noted prevent use of the truck.
scan.freshness_note: Log is current as of September 17, 2026 (10 days old as of the reference date of September 27, 2026). This is a live record and should continue to be updated with each shift.

gaps.title: No maintenance action or repair record
gaps.description: On September 9, the horn failed inspection ('X' in Horn column). The log does not indicate whether the defect was reported, when it was corrected, or on what date the truck was returned to service. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) requires that 'defects when found shall be immediately reported and corrected.' The log does not show how defects are tracked to closure.
gaps.fix: Add a 'Defect/Repair' column or supplementary log to document what defect was found, when it was reported, the date maintenance was completed, and the date the truck was cleared to return to service. Cross-reference defects in the pre-shift log to repair records.
gaps.locator: page 1, September 9 row; not addressed in document

gaps.title: No retention of signed or certified inspection records
gaps.description: The log shows operator initials (M.C., J.R.) but does not show dates of certification or evaluator names. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(l) requires the employer to maintain certification records with the operator's name, evaluation date, and evaluator's name. The current log does not serve as the certification record itself and provides no evidence that the operators have been formally trained and certified as required.
gaps.fix: Maintain separate operator certification records (not necessarily on this log) that document for each operator: (1) their full name, (2) the date they were evaluated and found competent, and (3) the name of the person who performed the evaluation. These records must be kept on file and must show re-evaluation at least every three years. The initials on this log should correspond to certified operators documented in those records.
gaps.locator: page 1, Operator column; certification records not in document

gaps.title: No documentation of safety training on inspection procedures
gaps.description: The document references 'Inspection per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7)' but does not show that operators have been trained on what to inspect, how to conduct the inspection, or what to do if a defect is found. OSHA requires that training cover vehicle inspection and maintenance that the operator will perform.
gaps.fix: Maintain training records documenting that each operator has received instruction on the pre-shift inspection procedures, the checklist items, how to perform each check, and the authority to remove an unsafe truck from service. This can be part of the initial operator certification training.
gaps.locator: page 1, header; training records not in document

gaps.title: No documentation of action taken after defect found
gaps.description: September 9 shows a horn defect, but the log does not indicate whether the truck was taken out of service, repaired, or when it returned to use. The header states 'do not use if a defect affects safety,' but there is no record showing compliance with this instruction in the case of the horn failure.
gaps.fix: When a defect is marked with 'X', document: (1) immediately remove truck from service, (2) notify supervisor/maintenance, (3) tag or lock the truck, (4) make repairs, (5) re-inspect the repaired component, and (6) clear the truck for return to service. A supplementary defect log should cross-reference to the pre-shift log and show these steps.
gaps.quote: do not use if a defect affects safety

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in the identity of this document as an inspection log and in what it records. The document is readable and the checklist items and operator initials are clear. Confidence is moderate-to-high that the horn defect on September 9 was not closed out on this log—no re-check or maintenance note appears. I am certain the log does not contain operator certification records; those are a separate requirement. I am not certain whether maintenance records for the horn or tank change are held elsewhere. The document references 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) accurately, but I searched to confirm the current text of that regulation and it matches. I did not locate Oregon-specific additions to the federal OSHA standard for powered industrial trucks, and I assume the federal standard is the binding one for Oregon OSHA (Oregon generally adopts federal OSHA standards); however, I have not verified whether Oregon DEQ has authority over this equipment or these inspections beyond what federal OSHA covers. The status is 'recorded' because this is a log of completed inspections, not an evaluation against a standard. The gaps are real and material: the lack of closure on defects and the absence of operator certification records create regulatory exposure.
